findings.title: raw_html posts are stored and rendered without any sanitization
findings.body: When cook_method is raw_html, cook returns the raw text unchanged, skipping the markdown pipeline, any sanitizer and the after_post_cook plugin filters. Imported content (RSS items via PollFeed, scraped pages via TopicEmbed.import_remote) is stored this way (topic_embed.rb:22), and PostCreator accepts cook_method from any caller's options with no whitelist (post_creator.rb:216). The cooked value is then emitted unescaped: embed/best.html.erb:19 uses 'raw post.cooked', and normal topic views render cooked as HTML. Any markup that reaches a raw_html post, such as a script tag in a feed item, runs as stored XSS on the forum's own origin for every visitor. Remote HTML needs sanitizing before it is stored as cooked.

findings.title: CGI.unescapeHTML turns escaped feed markup into live HTML
findings.body: RSS and Atom descriptions are almost always entity-escaped (a script tag appears as <script>). After CGI.unescapeHTML those entities become real markup. The result is saved with cook_method raw_html (topic_embed.rb:22) and rendered unescaped (see post.rb:133 and embed/best.html.erb:19), so any feed item can inject script into the forum for all visitors. Escaped content should stay escaped, or be sanitized, never unescaped.

findings.title: Article URL interpolated unescaped into stored HTML footer
findings.body: The URL is placed unescaped into an href attribute and a text node of the footer, which is then stored as raw HTML. The only check is that the URL starts with http(s):// (line 11). Characters such as single quote, equals and parentheses are legal in URL paths and can pass URI parsing, so a feed link like http://example.com/'onmouseover='alert(1) produces an anchor with an injected event handler. The URL should be HTML-escaped before interpolation.

findings.title: '<%- end if %>' is a syntax error; the best view cannot render
findings.body: The block opened on line 2 is closed with 'end if', which is not valid ERB/Ruby for closing a conditional. It compiles to 'end if ;', where the modifier 'if' has no condition, so the template raises SyntaxError whenever it is rendered. Every request for an existing embedded topic (the @topic_view branch) fails. It should be '<%- end %>'.

findings.title: Unauthenticated requests can trigger a full feed download and reimport each time
findings.body: The throttle is keyed on the full embed_url (lines 26-28). Only the host must match embeddable_host, so a client can vary the path or query string to get a fresh key every time. Each new key then calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute here, which downloads the entire feed and re-imports every item (poll_feed.rb:29, 31-36). The feed fetch and the readability fetch (topic_embed.rb:48) use open() with no timeout. An attacker can therefore keep Sidekiq workers busy with unbounded outbound fetches and DB writes. The feed poll needs its own global throttle or should not run inline per URL.

findings.title: A retrieve job is enqueued on every request; the throttle only runs inside the job
findings.body: When no topic exists, every request enqueues a retrieve_topic job, and the 60-second throttle is checked only when the job runs (topic_retriever.rb:27-28). Anonymous requests, and the loading page that reloads every 30 seconds, therefore create unbounded queue entries even when the URL was retrieved moments ago. The throttle check should happen before enqueueing, or duplicate jobs should be deduplicated.

findings.title: PostCreator enqueues jobs inside an open transaction
findings.body: PostCreator.create is called inside the outer Topic.transaction (line 21). PostCreator.create calls enqueue_jobs before returning, which queues process_post and feature_topic_users. Its own comment (post_creator.rb around line 290) says jobs must be enqueued after commit. With Sidekiq, a worker can start before this transaction commits and find no post, so the job silently does nothing. The TopicEmbed row is also created after those jobs are queued.

findings.title: ALLOWALL is not a valid X-Frame-Options value
findings.body: The only valid values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN and ALLOW-FROM. Browsers ignore unrecognized values, so this line only appears to allow framing by accident, and it overwrites any app-wide frame policy with a meaningless string. To allow framing, the header should be removed (for example response.headers.delete('X-Frame-Options')), not set to an invalid value.

findings.title: Origin check uses substring match, so look-alike origins are accepted
findings.body: discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 checks whether the sender origin is a substring of discourseUrl, not whether it equals it. If discourseUrl is 'https://forum.example.com/', a page at 'https://forum.example.co' passes the check and can send 'discourse-resize' messages. The impact is limited to setting the iframe height, but this is the only origin validation in the embed script and it is wrong. The comparison should parse discourseUrl and compare origins for equality.

findings.title: One bad feed item aborts the whole poll; nil content is not guarded
findings.body: The loop has no per-item rescue. If any item raises (for example i.content is nil, which is possible for entries with only a summary, so nil.scrub raises; or TopicEmbed.import raises on a PostCreator or permission error), the remaining items are never imported. The job is also scheduled with retry: false, so the failure is dropped until the next hourly run hits the same item again.

findings.title: Shipped migration now uses force: true, which drops an existing table
findings.body: This changes an existing migration to create_table with force: true. If top_topics already exists with data in any environment where the migration version is not recorded (for example a database built from another branch), this migration drops the table and all its rows without warning. The flag is not needed for a table this migration is supposed to create for the first time and should be removed.

findings.title: --category option removed with no replacement and no documentation
findings.body: The method_option :category and its only use are deleted. Existing invocations that pass --category or -c now fail with an unknown-option error. The import also changes behaviour: the topic is now built by scraping the article with readability (TopicEmbed.import_remote) instead of a permalink post, and created_at is no longer set on the topic. The PR description is only 'Test 4', so none of this is documented.

findings.title: Gate tests pass for the wrong reason; poll_feed itself is untested
findings.body: feed_polling_enabled defaults to false (site_settings.yml). The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' examples never enable feed_polling_enabled, so execute returns early at the first gate and the expectation holds regardless of the gate under test. Only the 'delegates' example enables all three, and it mocks poll_feed. The actual import loop, nil handling and failure behaviour have no coverage.

findings.title: Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten to a wrong absolute URL
findings.body: An href like //cdn.example.com/a.png starts with '/', so the sub(/^\/+/, '') strips both slashes and the result is prefix + '/cdn.example.com/a.png', i.e. http://host/cdn.example.com/a.png. The same problem exists for img src (line 71). Protocol-relative links should keep their host, or be resolved with URI.join against the article URL.

findings.title: Adding a NOT NULL column with a default rewrites the posts table under lock
findings.body: On PostgreSQL releases before 11, add_column with default: 1 and null: false rewrites the entire posts table while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. On a large forum this blocks all reads and writes to posts for the duration. The safer pattern is to add the column nullable, backfill in batches, then set the default and NOT NULL constraint.

findings.title: setnx and expire are not atomic; a crash leaves the throttle key without a TTL
findings.body: The key is set with setnx and then given a 60-second expiry in a separate command. If the process dies between the two, the key never expires and that embed URL is throttled permanently for non-staff users. A single atomic SET with NX and EX options would avoid this.

findings.title: URL validation uses ^ instead of \A, so it matches any line
findings.body: In Ruby, ^ matches at the start of any line. A value such as 'javascript:alert(1)' followed by a newline and 'http://x' passes this check. The later URI() call in absolutize_urls currently rejects it, so no harm follows, but the validation is ineffective and relies on an unrelated exception. The regex should be anchored with \A.

findings.title: Test name says 404 but asserts only non-success; referer mismatch is untested
findings.body: The example 'is 404 without an embed_url' does not set a host, so it fails on the host check and never exercises the missing-parameter path. It only asserts not-success, so it does not verify a 404. There is also no example for a referer whose host differs from embeddable_host, which is the main access check in ensure_embeddable.

findings.title: Spec asserts raw HTML is stored and rendered verbatim
findings.body: The assertion post.cooked.should == post.raw locks in the behaviour that imported content is stored as-is with no sanitization. Nothing tests escaping of the article URL in the footer, sanitization of feed or scraped HTML, the unchanged-content update path, or import_remote. The security-relevant paths of this feature are not covered.
